estimand_functional: \(\mathcal R(C)=\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}\), with \(\mathsf S(E)=(\operatorname{skel}(G_E),\operatorname{uc}(G_E),(\mathcal N_j(E))_{j\in V},F(E))\)

sampling_model.design: Population equality of full positive-definite covariance models is the identification kernel; the statistical rung uses independent Gaussian sampling and global BIC over the finite labelled state class.
sampling_model.units: Each observation is one independent realization of the \(p\)-variable centered linear Gaussian SEM.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment in the structure-identification theorem; the prespecified pairs in \(\mathcal Q\) index downstream interventions and responses.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; every innovation variance is positive and otherwise unrestricted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For each candidate state and positive-definite sample covariance, target-local block-incidence matrices define positive-definite Gram systems whose unique solutions estimate the common coefficient in each parent block; strictly positive constrained residual variances estimate the innovation variances. The effect maps apply these same off-model block-constrained solutions before taking finite path sums and derivatives. A deterministic measurable fallback invokes no Gram inverse, likelihood supremum, or derivative when \(S_n\) is singular, and all asymptotic claims run through integers \(n\geq p\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.17 proves structural identifiability within BPEC-DAGs, whose edge-colour classes all have size at least two, while Question 5.19 asks for a graphical characterization of edge-coloured model equivalence.
Theorem 2 transforms any pair of equivalent DAGs through exactly their distinct disagreeing edges, each reversed while covered.
Theorem 4.1 characterizes partial-homoscedastic model equivalence by ordinary Markov equivalence and fixed parent sets for vertices in nonsingleton variance blocks.
Theorem 4.4 characterizes existence and uniqueness of the MLE in a fixed compatibly coloured RDAG through augmented-sample linear independence.
The essential graph uniquely represents each ordinary DAG Markov-equivalence class and has chordal chain components.
The paper gives polynomial-time counting and uniform sampling for ordinary Markov equivalence classes by clique-picking on chordal components.
The paper gives linear-delay enumeration of ordinary Markov-equivalent DAGs, including fixed-background-knowledge variants.
The paper establishes BIC-type asymptotic model choice for finitely many smoothly curved submodels of an exponential family.
IDA consistently estimates the multiset of possible total effects across an ordinary Markov-equivalence class.
The paper constructs resampling-and-screening confidence intervals for one fixed true causal effect after constraint-based graph discovery.
The paper derives efficient least-squares estimators and joint covariance calculations for total effects under a known linear causal graph.

tldr: Equal incoming coefficients encode communities of direct causes. BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 makes those communities structurally identifiable by excluding singleton blocks, but admitting singleton causes restores genuine observational equivalence and leaves the correct quotient unknown. The project characterizes equality of the full positive-definite covariance models exactly: two target-blocked states agree if and only if their skeletons, unshielded colliders, repeated parent blocks, and orientations across unequal endpoint block families agree, equivalently if and only if singleton-block covered reversals with partition transport connect them. Tangent-support recovery and an exact sparse covariance separator supply the coefficient-specific necessity; Chickering's monotone transformation then yields a shortest path. The same quotient gives complete finite enumeration, generic fixed-\(p\) BIC component recovery, and simultaneous inference for its finite set of total effects, while output-sensitive enumeration of distinct rational effect maps remains open.

project_justification.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 proves BPEC structural identifiability only after forbidding singleton edge-colour classes and explicitly leaves graphical and transformational edge-coloured equivalence open. Ordinary covered reversals ignore coefficient partitions, while partial homoscedasticity constrains innovation variances rather than incoming coefficients.
project_justification.niche: Target-local blocked colourings with unrestricted positive noise variances form a natural intermediate class: repeated blocks reveal stable causal communities, but singleton blocks retain exactly the ordinary orientation ambiguity compatible with those communities.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the repeated-block invariant from the model tangent at the identity, proves by a sparse regression separator that reversed edges must join equal endpoint families, and combines these facts with monotone covered reversals to obtain an if-and-only-if static and transformational characterization plus its statistical quotient consequences.

related_work: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 is the writing and primary method anchor: its Introduction frames equal incoming coefficients as causal communities, Theorem 4.1 proves smooth model geometry, Proposition 5.4 and Corollary 5.6 provide edge-colour faithfulness, Theorem 5.17 proves identifiability only for proper blocked colourings, and Questions 5.19--5.20 plus the Discussion leave graphical and transformational equivalence open. Chickering1995, Theorem 2 and its Find-Edge proof, supplies the disagreement-decreasing sequence of distinct covered reversals; the new first step is proving every selected arrow is a singleton block and its endpoint partitions coincide on common parents. WuDrton2023, Theorem 4.1, is the closest complete partition-constrained analogue: it fixes parent sets at vertices sharing a nonsingleton innovation-variance block, whereas the present invariant recovers labelled repeated incoming coefficient blocks and orientations across unequal endpoint families. MakamReichenbachSeigal2023 studies likelihood geometry and least-squares MLEs for a fixed compatibly coloured RDAG, not equality of covariance images across graph orientations. AnderssonMadiganPerlman1997 and the two 2023 Wienobst papers provide ordinary essential-graph, counting, and enumeration machinery; transported target partitions are absent. Haughton1988 informs the finite smooth-model BIC argument, with exact-image quotienting and algebraic intersection removal derived here. MaathuisKalischBuhlmann2009, ChangGuoMalinsky2026, and GuoPerkovic2022EfficientLS inform possible-effect estimation and post-discovery inference, but do not cover every member of a blocked full-model-equivalence effect set.
technical_internal_limitation: The population component \(\mathcal R(C)\) is an equivalence class of complete covariance-model images, not the pointwise fibre of every state fitting one exceptional covariance. Zero edges and coincident coefficients can create additional pointwise representations outside the component. The fixed directed set \(F(C)\) records orientations forced directly by unequal nonsingleton families, but ordinary collider and acyclicity constraints can compel further arrows. Neither fact identifies a numerical coefficient merely because its arrow is compelled.
honest_scope: The equivalence theorem concerns finite labelled causally sufficient linear Gaussian DAGs, target-local coefficient blocks, unrestricted real block coefficients, unrestricted positive target-specific innovation variances, and full positive-definite covariance images. It does not cover cross-target edge colours, vertex-coloured innovation variances, latent confounding, selection, cycles, or pointwise supermodel fibres. The BIC and confidence procedures use deterministic measurable fallbacks at singular sample covariance, while their limits concern integers \(n\geq p\), for which \(S_n\) is positive definite almost surely. These results are fixed-\(p\), pointwise, and generic away from a proper algebraic exceptional set; no greedy-search consistency or uniform inference near model intersections is asserted. In the all-singleton case the exact reduction is ordinary DAG Markov equivalence, and in the no-singleton case the component is a singleton.

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Number of labelled system variables.

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: Common vertex set of every graph under comparison.

symbols.name: pa
symbols.def: Parents of vertex \(j\) in a directed graph \(K\) on \(V\).

symbols.name: Kgraph
symbols.def: Generic directed graph used in the state-class definition.

symbols.def: Generic family of target-specific parent partitions.

symbols.def: Generic candidate state used only as the bound member of the blocked-state class.

symbols.def: All labelled acyclic graphs on \(V\) equipped with a partition of each target's parent set, including singleton blocks.

symbols.def: Directed acyclic graph coordinate of \(E\).

symbols.name: betaE

symbols.name: BE

symbols.name: C

symbols.name: Pi

symbols.def: Partition coordinate of \(D\).

symbols.name: UC

symbols.name: Sig

symbols.name: Tspace

symbols.def: Breadth-first traversal from \(C\) applying every defined legal reversal and memoizing each labelled graph-partition state.

symbols.name: n

symbols.name: BIC
symbols.sig: \[\operatorname{BIC}_n(E)=\begin{cases}-2\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal M(E)}\ell_n(\Sigma)+d_E\log n,&S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++},\\ d_E\log n,&S_n\notin\mathbb S^p_{++},\end{cases}\qquad d_E=p+\sum_{j\in V}|\Pi^E_j|.\]
symbols.def: Total Gaussian BIC criterion with the likelihood branch used only for positive-definite sample covariance and a deterministic measurable fallback otherwise.

symbols.name: Chat
symbols.def: Any global BIC minimizer under a deterministic tie rule.

symbols.name: Exc
symbols.def: Finite union of pullbacks of intersections with nonequivalent blocked covariance models of dimension at most \(d_C\), together with zero-gradient effect strata.

symbols.name: Qpairs
symbols.def: Prespecified ordered pairs for which total effects are reported.

symbols.name: Sigma
symbols.def: Argument of the off-model block-constrained least-squares maps.

symbols.name: BlockInc
symbols.def: With rows indexed by \(i\in P_{Ej}\) and columns indexed by \(B\in\Pi^E_j\), \((A_{Ej})_{iB}=\mathbf 1\{i\in B\}\).

symbols.name: BlockGram
symbols.def: Gram matrix of the block-sum regressors for target \(j\); it is positive definite whenever \(P_{Ej}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\).

symbols.name: BlockScore
symbols.def: Covariance vector between the block-sum regressors and target \(j\).

symbols.name: LE
symbols.def: For each target \(j\) with nonempty parent set, solve \(\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)\beta_{Ej}(\Sigma)=h_{Ej}(\Sigma)\), repeat the block coefficient \(\beta_{Ej,B}(\Sigma)\) on every \(i\in B\), and put zero outside the parent set; the empty-parent row is zero.

symbols.name: gEffect
symbols.def: For state \(E\) and positive-definite \(\Sigma\), apply the explicit target-local block-constrained map \(L_E(\Sigma)\) and take its path-sum total effects. The map is rational and smooth throughout \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\).

symbols.name: EffectSet
symbols.sig: \(\mathcal T_E(\Sigma)=\{g_D(\Sigma):D\in\mathcal R(E)\}\) for \(E\in\mathfrak S_p\) and \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\)
symbols.def: Finite plug-in effect set on the positive-definite cone; at \(E=C\) and \(\Sigma\in\mathcal M(C)\) it is the component's causal-effect target.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Familywise noncoverage level.

symbols.name: Conf
symbols.def: On \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), the Bonferroni collection uses the explicit block-constrained maps \(L_E(S_n)\), the resulting rational effect maps, and their delta-method derivatives on the positive-definite cone; on \(S_n\notin\mathbb S^p_{++}\), it is the deterministic collection of full real-line intervals.

symbols.name: Henum
symbols.def: Technique handle combining the fixed-edge essential graph induced by \(\mathsf S(C)\), chordal clique-picking, partition-compatible orientation tests, and symbolic equality testing of member effect functionals.

assumptions.condition: The directed graph \(\mathcal K\) is acyclic.
For every \(j\in V\), \(\Xi_j\) is a partition of \(\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal K}(j)\), with singleton blocks permitted.

standard.name: Blocked target-local edge colouring with the singleton-allowing variant

definitions.name: BlockedStateClass
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak S_p=\left\{A=(\mathcal K,\Xi):\mathcal K\text{ is an acyclic directed graph on }V,\ \Xi_j\text{ is a partition of }\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal K}(j)\text{ for every }j\in V\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Full blocked covariance model
definitions.construction: For \(E\in\mathfrak S_p\), let \(b_E=\sum_{j\in V}|\Pi^E_j|\), \(\Theta_E=\mathbb R^{b_E}\times(0,\infty)^p\), and \[\mathcal M(E)=\left\{(I_p-B_E(\beta_E))^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_E)(I_p-B_E(\beta_E))^{-\mathsf T}:(\beta_E,\omega_E)\in\Theta_E\right\}.\] Here \(B_E(\beta_E)_{ji}=\beta_{jB}\) for \(i\in B\in\Pi^E_j\), and all real block coefficients are admitted.

definitions.name: Off-diagonal model tangent
definitions.construction: At \(I_p\in\mathcal M(E)\), define \[T_E^{\circ}=\operatorname{proj}_{\mathrm{off}}T_{I_p}\mathcal M(E)=\operatorname{span}\{v_{jB}:j\in V,\ B\in\Pi^E_j\},\qquad \operatorname{supp}(v_{jB})=\{\{i,j\}:i\in B\}.\]

definitions.name: Partition-compatible singleton covered reversal
definitions.construction: For \(i\to j\) in \(G_E\), \(\operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}(E)\) is defined exactly when \(\operatorname{pa}_{G_E}(j)=\operatorname{pa}_{G_E}(i)\cup\{i\}\), \(\{i\}\in\Pi^E_j\), and \(\Pi^E_j\setminus\{\{i\}\}=\Pi^E_i\). It reverses \(i\to j\), sets \(\Pi'_j=\Pi^E_i\) and \(\Pi'_i=\Pi^E_i\cup\{\{j\}\}\), and leaves every other partition unchanged.

definitions.name: Legal-reversal component
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal R(E)=\{E'\in\mathfrak S_p:E'\text{ is reached from }E\text{ by a finite sequence of defined }\operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}\}.\]

definitions.name: Complete breadth-first component enumerator
definitions.construction: Initialize a queue and visited set with \(C\). Repeatedly remove the first state, test every oriented edge for the conditions in \(\texttt{def:legal-reversal}\), append every unvisited resulting state, and terminate when the queue is empty; the emitted visited set is \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)\).

definitions.name: Off-model target-local block-constrained least-squares map
definitions.construction: Fix \(E\in\mathfrak S_p\), \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), and \(j\in V\). Write \(P_{Ej}=\operatorname{pa}_{G_E}(j)\), and let \(A_{Ej}\) have rows \(i\in P_{Ej}\), columns \(B\in\Pi^E_j\), and entries \((A_{Ej})_{iB}=\mathbf 1\{i\in B\}\). If \(P_{Ej}\neq\varnothing\), define \[\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)=A_{Ej}^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{P_{Ej},P_{Ej}}A_{Ej},\qquad h_{Ej}(\Sigma)=A_{Ej}^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{P_{Ej},j},\qquad \beta_{Ej}(\Sigma)=\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)^{-1}h_{Ej}(\Sigma).\] The columns of \(A_{Ej}\) are linearly independent because \(\Pi^E_j\) is a partition into nonempty blocks, so \(\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)\) is positive definite and the solution is unique. Set \((L_E(\Sigma))_{ji}=\beta_{Ej,B}(\Sigma)\) for \(i\in B\in\Pi^E_j\) and zero for \(i\notin P_{Ej}\); if \(P_{Ej}=\varnothing\), take the unique empty coefficient vector and set row \(j\) to zero. Thus \(L_E(\Sigma)\) is defined for every \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), is rational in the entries of \(\Sigma\), and is smooth on the positive-definite cone.

definitions.name: Global blocked-state BIC
definitions.construction: For each \(E\in\mathfrak S_p\), set \(d_E=p+\sum_{j\in V}|\Pi^E_j|\). On the measurable event \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), compute \(L_E(S_n)\) using the block-design systems in \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\). For each target set \(\widehat\omega_{Ej}=S_{n,jj}-h_{Ej}(S_n)^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_{Ej}(S_n)^{-1}h_{Ej}(S_n)\), with \(\widehat\omega_{Ej}=S_{n,jj}\) for an empty parent set. Positive definiteness of \(S_n\) makes every nonempty \(\Gamma_{Ej}(S_n)\) positive definite and every \(\widehat\omega_{Ej}\) strictly positive, so the Gaussian likelihood supremum is finite and attained and \[\operatorname{BIC}_n(E)=-2\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal M(E)}\ell_n(\Sigma)+d_E\log n.\] On \(S_n\notin\mathbb S^p_{++}\), invoke no Gram inverse, residual-variance formula, or likelihood supremum and set \(\operatorname{BIC}_n(E)=d_E\log n\). For every \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(\widehat C_n\) be the minimizer over \(\mathfrak S_p\) selected by a fixed deterministic ordering of states.

definitions.name: Generic component-selection exception
definitions.construction: For \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), let \(\mathcal E_C\subsetneq\Theta_C\) be the finite union, over \(D\in\mathfrak S_p\) with \(d_D\leq d_C\) and \(\mathcal M(D)\neq\mathcal M(C)\), of the polynomial pullbacks of \(\mathcal M(C)\cap\mathcal M(D)\), augmented by the polynomial zero-gradient loci of the reported nonconstant effect coordinates.

definitions.name: Component total-effect set
definitions.construction: For \(E\in\mathfrak S_p\) and \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), compute the explicit block-constrained map \(L_D(\Sigma)\) from \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\) for every \(D\in\mathcal R(E)\). Define \(g_D(\Sigma)=(((I_p-L_D(\Sigma))^{-1})_{ya})_{(a,y)\in\mathcal Q}\) and \[\mathcal T_E(\Sigma)=\{g_D(\Sigma):D\in\mathcal R(E)\}.\] Because \(G_D\) is acyclic, \(I_p-L_D(\Sigma)\) is invertible. Each \(g_D\) is rational and smooth on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\), and \(\mathrm Dg_D(\Sigma)\) is defined throughout that cone. The causal target is the specialization \(\mathcal T_C(\Sigma)\) for \(\Sigma\in\mathcal M(C)\).

definitions.name: Simultaneous component-effect confidence collection
definitions.construction: For every \(n\in\mathbb N\), first select \(\widehat C_n\) by \(\texttt{def:global-bic}\). On \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), order the finite member-labelled coordinates \(g_E(S_n)\) for \(E\in\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)\), compute every \(L_E(S_n)\) through the block-design Gram system in \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\), and evaluate the derivative \(\mathrm Dg_E(S_n)\) of the rational map in \(\texttt{def:component-effect-set}\) only on this open positive-definite domain. Use these derivatives with the plug-in Gaussian sample-covariance covariance matrix to obtain delta-method standard errors. Let \(K\) be the number of nonconstant labelled coordinates. If \(K\geq1\), use critical value \(z_{1-\alpha/(2K)}\) for those coordinates and report structurally zero coordinates as singleton intervals; if \(K=0\), report only the singleton intervals and do not evaluate a critical value. On \(S_n\notin\mathbb S^p_{++}\), invoke no Gram inverse, coefficient map, or delta-method derivative and assign the interval \(\mathbb R\) to every member-labelled coordinate. The resulting total measurable collection is \(\mathfrak I_{n,\alpha}(\widehat C_n)\).

definitions.name: Partition-aware clique-picking handle
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{enum}}\): begin from the ordinary essential graph of \(G\), insert the orientations in \(F(C)\) as background constraints, adapt chordal clique-picking so every orientation is checked against transported parent partitions, and quotient emitted states by symbolic equality of the rational maps \(g_E\).

statements.statement: For any \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\), equality \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\) implies equality of their skeletons and \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for every \(j\in V\). More precisely, the inclusion-minimal nonempty supports in \(T_C^{\circ}\) are exactly \(\{\{i,j\}:i\in B\}\) for \(B\in\Pi_j\); every support of size at least two has a unique center \(j\) and recovers the labelled block \(B\), while a support of size one recovers only the underlying edge. Thus every edge whose orientation differs between \(G\) and \(H\) is a singleton block in both states.
statements.justification: The tangent support partition is the first orientation-robust observable that distinguishes repeated incoming coefficient blocks from reversible singleton edges.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Theorem 4.1 and Section 5, gives smoothness and fixed-graph rational recovery but no cross-DAG recovery of target-local blocks from equality of model images.
statements.consumer: The lemma lets a covariance-model comparison recover causal communities without knowing which Markov-equivalent orientation generated them.

statements.statement: Let \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\) satisfy \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\), and suppose \(x\to y\) is in \(G\) while \(y\to x\) is in \(H\). Then \(\mathcal N_x(C)=\mathcal N_y(C)\). Specifically, if \(S\in\mathcal N_x(C)\) is split across two blocks of \(\Pi_y\), choosing unit innovation variances, coefficient one on \(x\to y\), coefficient one on a block \(T\in\Pi_y\) meeting but not containing \(S\), and zero elsewhere gives a covariance in \(\mathcal M(C)\) whose regression of \(X_x\) on \(\operatorname{pa}_H(x)\) has coefficient \(-q\mathbf 1\{s\in T\}\) on \(s\in S\), with \(q=(2+|T\setminus(\operatorname{pa}_H(x)\setminus\{y\})|)^{-1}>0\), contradicting the block \(S\) in \(D\).
statements.justification: This sparse covariance witness is the load-bearing necessity step because it handles arbitrary extra target parents and simultaneous arrow changes.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Lemma 5.11 and the proof of Theorem 5.17, separates reversals only in the proper-colouring regime; it does not establish the endpoint-family condition when singleton blocks coexist with repeated blocks.
statements.consumer: The separator certifies when a proposed singleton reversal changes the complete covariance model, preventing a learner from merging observationally distinguishable causal-community states.

statements.statement: For every \(C=(G,\Pi),D=(H,\Lambda)\in\mathfrak S_p\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\); \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\), equivalently \(G,H\) have the same skeleton and unshielded colliders, \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for all \(j\in V\), and every edge joining vertices with unequal nonsingleton families has the same orientation; and \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\). Every step in the final characterization is a partition-compatible singleton covered reversal with the prescribed transport. Moreover, \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D)\), and a shortest path reverses each disagreeing arrow exactly once. When every block is nonsingleton, \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\), recovering and strictly extending the BPEC structural-identifiability result of BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 to the singleton-allowing blocked class.
statements.justification: The theorem supplies both an exact static recovery functional and a complete local transformation calculus for the largest target-blocked coefficient class that contains ordinary DAG equivalence.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Theorem 5.17, excludes singleton edge-colour classes and Question 5.19 asks for graphical edge-coloured equivalence; Chickering1995, Theorem 2, transports ordinary DAGs but has no coefficient-partition legality condition.
statements.consumer: An extension of the colouredDAGs workflow can report the exact covariance-equivalence component instead of one arbitrary blocked DAG while retaining all repeated-coefficient communities.

statements.statement: For every \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)=\mathcal R(C)=\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}\). Static equality can be decided using \(O(p^3)\) elementary comparisons with adjacency matrices and canonical block bitsets. The enumeration is duplicate-free by exact state memoization, terminates after at most \(p!\) emitted states, and a breadth-first predecessor tree returns for every emitted \(D\) a shortest path of length \(\delta(C,D)\).
statements.justification: The population equivalence theorem becomes operational only after it yields a terminating complete enumerator and shortest certificates.
statements.gap: WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023 gives linear-delay enumeration for ordinary Markov classes with fixed background knowledge, but does not handle state-dependent partition transport; the present guaranteed algorithm is finite and output-bounded rather than linear-delay.
statements.consumer: Component enumeration supplies every graph-specific adjustment and path functional needed for possible-effect analysis under blocked coefficient information.

statements.statement: If every block of \(C\) is a singleton, then \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\varnothing\) for all \(j\) and \(\mathcal R(C)\) is exactly the ordinary Markov-equivalence class of \(G\), with \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}=\delta\) as in Chickering1995. If no block of \(C\) is a singleton, then every edge is fixed and \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\) as in the BPEC identifiability boundary. If \(G=H\) and \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\), then \(\Pi=\Lambda\).
statements.justification: The two extreme partitions verify that the characterization interpolates exactly between ordinary Markov equivalence and proper blocked identifiability.
statements.gap: The two endpoint results are published separately by Chickering1995 and BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026; their exact interpolation within one full-model criterion is new.
statements.consumer: These reductions provide regression tests for software and prevent interpreting every fixed arrow as a numerically identified direct effect.

statements.statement: Fix \(p\), \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), and a parameter \(\theta_C\in\Theta_C\setminus\mathcal E_C\) with \(\Sigma_0=\phi_C(\theta_C)\). For each integer \(n\geq p\), let \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\) be independent \(N_p(0,\Sigma_0)\) observations and let \(\widehat C_n\) be the deterministically tie-broken global minimizer in \(\texttt{def:global-bic}\). Then \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\) almost surely. Consequently every statewise block Gram matrix \(\Gamma_{Ej}(S_n)\) is invertible, every constrained residual variance in \(\texttt{def:global-bic}\) is strictly positive, and only the finite attained likelihood branch is used. As \(n\to\infty\) through integers satisfying \(n\geq p\), \[\Pr\{\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\}\longrightarrow1.\] The exceptional set is proper algebraic: models of dimension at most \(d_C\) are excluded by their nonzero pulled-back defining polynomials, while larger models lose by the diverging dimension penalty. This is component recovery, not consistency of greedy GECS.
statements.justification: Singleton blocks change the estimable structural target from one state to an exact quotient component, so selection consistency must quotient identical covariance images.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Section 6 and Discussion, derives a decomposable BIC and reports GECS simulations but leaves consistency open; Haughton1988 treats finitely many smooth models without the blocked-state equality quotient.
statements.consumer: A fixed-dimensional coloured-DAG analysis can consistently report the right component even when several singleton-block orientations have exactly equal likelihood.

statements.statement: Under the conditions of \(\texttt{thm:generic-bic-component-recovery}\), fix finite \(\mathcal Q\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). Along integers \(n\geq p\), the event \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\) has probability one. Hence every \(L_E(S_n)\) is obtained from the uniquely solvable block-constrained Gram systems in \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\), and every derivative \(\mathrm D g_E(S_n)\) is evaluated inside the positive-definite cone on which \(g_E\) is rational and smooth. Then \(\mathcal T_{\widehat C_n}(S_n)\) converges in probability to \(\mathcal T_C(\Sigma_0)\) in Hausdorff distance. With \(\mathfrak I_{n,\alpha}(\widehat C_n)\) defined memberwise before removing numerical duplicates, \[\liminf_{\substack{n\to\infty\\ n\geq p}}\Pr\left\{\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\text{ and }g_E(\Sigma_0)\text{ belongs to its labelled interval in }\mathfrak I_{n,\alpha}(\widehat C_n)\text{ for every }E\in\mathcal R(C)\right\}\geq1-\alpha.\] The conclusion permits coincident effect values and singular joint covariance because only marginal nonconstant-coordinate variances enter the Bonferroni construction.
statements.justification: The observationally identified object is a finite set of possible effects, so valid inference must cover all component members rather than one selected graph.
statements.gap: MaathuisKalischBuhlmann2009 proves consistency of possible-effect multisets without simultaneous intervals, while ChangGuoMalinsky2026 targets coverage of one fixed true effect after graph screening rather than every member of a full-model-equivalence effect set.
statements.consumer: An analyst using the Sachs protein network can report simultaneous uncertainty for every total effect compatible with the recovered coefficient-community component.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{enum}}\), can one construct an output-polynomial or polynomial-delay algorithm that emits each distinct rational total-effect functional \(g_E\), for \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\), exactly once and returns a certificate partitioning all states by functional equality, while preserving the shortest legal-reversal certificates from \(C\)? The construction must derive path independence of transported partitions and may not assume that numerically coincident evaluations identify equal rational functionals.
statements.justification: State enumeration can be exponentially more redundant than the causal output, and symbolic duplicate removal is the nonroutine bridge from a structural class to usable possible-effect analysis.
statements.gap: WienobstBannachLiskiewicz2023 counts ordinary Markov-equivalent DAGs by clique-picking, and GuoPerkovic2022EfficientLS estimates effects for enumerated parent sets; neither quotients a transported-partition component by equality of rational effect maps.
statements.consumer: Large sparse components could feed IDA-style effect analysis without storing every observationally equivalent blocked state.
